tools.name: approve_mcp_server
tools.description:
Store an operator approval for exactly the tool definitions and launch identity the operator reviewed, so later vet_mcp_server calls treat them as approved and report any change as drift. The server must still pass every WARDEN gate; an approval cannot override a block.

When to use: after a human reviewed the output of status_mcp_server and agreed. Pass back the currentToolsHash, currentIdentityHash and previousRevision it returned; if the payload or the stored approval changed in the meantime, the call is refused and the review must be repeated.

When NOT to use: on your own initiative or to make a blocked server pass (the gates run again and the call fails); to remove an approval (revoke_mcp_server); to look at the stored state (status_mcp_server).

Behaviour: writes one file in the local state directory and replaces any earlier approval for this server id. Refused unless the operator started this process with WARDEN_ALLOW_PIN_CHANGES=1. No network; never starts the target server. Repeating the same call is refused because the revision it names is no longer current.

Returns { approved: true, pin }. Example: approve_mcp_server({ server, tools, reviewed_tools_hash: "<currentToolsHash>", reviewed_identity_hash: "<currentIdentityHash>", previous_pin_revision: null }).

id.description: Stable server id the host uses for pins and logs (e.g. "github@1"). Findings quote this id.

name.description: Human-facing server name. Threat-feed server-scope patterns match this field.

command.description: stdio executable (e.g. "npx"). Required for a realistic stdio identity hash; omit for url transports.

args.description: stdio argv. Included in the launch-identity hash used by pinning. Omit when unused.

url.description: sse/http endpoint. Threat-feed and identity hashing see this string; this tool does not request it.

catalog.description: Remote catalog this server was discovered from. When set and policy.allowUnknownServers is false, the origin gate fail-closes. Omit for operator-declared servers.

tools.description: The exact tools/list payload the operator reviewed. Its hash must equal reviewed_tools_hash.

outputSchema.description: Unmodified output schema, including nested descriptions; scanned and pinned.

tools.name: canonicalize_json
tools.description:
Return the RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme serialization WARDEN uses for threat-feed signatures and tool-def pins, so another implementation can byte-check against it. Integers only inside ±(2^53−1); lone surrogates and non-integers are refused with a reason code, not escaped.

When to use: you are publishing or verifying a signed threat feed, hashing tool defs, or comparing two JSON documents that must agree regardless of key order. Subpath @aimarket/warden/jcs is the same function.

When NOT to use: scanning tool defs (static_scan_tools); pretty-printing for humans (this output is for bytes, not display).

Behaviour: local, no network. Pass either a parsed JSON value or a JSON string (string is parsed with parseJsonStrict first). Failure returns isError with CanonicalizationCode — it does not emit partial bytes.

Returns { canonical } or an error. Example: canonicalize_json({ value: { b: 1, a: 2 } }) → {"a":2,"b":1}.

value.description: JSON value to canonicalize, or a JSON string to parse first. Objects have keys sorted by UTF-16 code units. Numbers must be integers in ±(2^53−1). Do not pass undefined, functions, or cyclic structures.

canonical.description: RFC 8785 canonical JSON text (UTF-8-ready string). Hash or sign these bytes, not JSON.stringify output.

tools.name: check_egress_url
tools.description:
Ask EgressGuard whether a URL's hostname is on an operator allowlist. A tool reaching a host you never listed is the classic phone-home tell. Empty allowlist blocks everything (fail-closed), not everything-allowed.

When to use: a tool is about to fetch/post and you want the same check a host should wrap around that request. Hostnames match case-insensitively; "*.example.com" matches subdomains, not the apex.

When NOT to use: vetting tool definitions (vet_mcp_server / static_scan_tools); canonicalizing JSON (canonicalize_json). This does not fetch the URL and does not inspect tool text.

Behaviour: local URL parse + hostname match. Unparseable URLs are refused. No DNS, no HTTP. Idempotent.

Returns { allowed, host?, reason? }. Example: check_egress_url({ url: "https://api.github.com/repos", allowlist: ["api.github.com", "*.internal.example.com"] }).

url.description: Absolute URL the tool wants to open (https://host/path). Only the hostname is compared; path, query, and credentials are not allowlisted separately. Must be parseable by the WHATWG URL parser.

allowlist.description: Permitted hostnames. Exact match, or leading "*." for subdomains ("*.example.com" matches api.example.com, not example.com). Empty array blocks every host. Entries are trimmed and compared case-insensitively.

allowed.description: true only when the hostname matches an allowlist entry.

host.description: Parsed hostname when the URL was valid.

reason.description: Why the request is blocked; omitted when allowed is true.

tools.name: classify_sensitive_tools
tools.description:
Split advertised tool names into sensitive vs safe using the operator's case-insensitive * globs (the same policy.sensitiveToolPatterns a host would use). Sensitive tools stay advertised; they require per-call approval — this tool does not run them.

When to use: show the user which names will need confirmation before they approve a server, or to preview a glob set. This is policy over identifiers, not an injection scan.

When NOT to use: scanning descriptions for poisoning (static_scan_tools or vet_mcp_server); checking whether a URL is allowed out (check_egress_url).

Behaviour: local glob match, no network. An empty patterns array marks every tool safe. Patterns match the whole name; "*delete*" hits create_delete_repo. Does not call Warden.vet and does not persist anything.

Returns { sensitive, safe }. Example: classify_sensitive_tools({ tools: [{ name: "delete_repo", description: "Delete a repository.", inputSchema: { type: "object" } }], patterns: ["*delete*"] }).
tools/list items whose names will be classified. Descriptions and schemas are ignored; only name is matched.

tools.name: revoke_mcp_server
tools.description:
Delete the stored approval for one server id. Afterwards vet_mcp_server treats the server as never seen: its tools are unpinned again until someone approves them anew.

When to use: an operator no longer trusts a server, or wants its next approval to start from a clean review. Take previousRevision from status_mcp_server first; the call is refused if the approval changed after that.

When NOT to use: to approve a changed server (approve_mcp_server replaces the old approval directly); to block a server for everyone (a revoked server is unpinned, not blocked — use a threat feed or policy for that); to inspect state (status_mcp_server).

Behaviour: deletes one file in the local state directory; cannot be undone except by approving again. Refused unless the operator started this process with WARDEN_ALLOW_PIN_CHANGES=1. Needs no tools payload. No network.

Returns { revoked: true, serverId }. Example: revoke_mcp_server({ server: { id: "demo@0", name: "demo", transport: "stdio", command: "npx" }, previous_pin_revision: "<previousRevision>" }).

anyOf.description: A stored approval: serverId, toolsHash, identityHash, approvalMode (operator | automatic), toolNames, the approved tool definitions and approvedAt.

previousRevision.description: sha256 of the stored approval; pass it as previous_pin_revision. null when nothing is stored.

currentToolsHash.description: Hash of the tools you passed; pass it as reviewed_tools_hash to approve exactly these definitions.

currentIdentityHash.description: Hash of the launch identity (transport, command, args, url, name); pass it as reviewed_identity_hash.

changed.description: true when an approval is stored and the tools or the launch identity differ from it.

currentTools.description: The tool definitions that were hashed, echoed for the operator's review.

numbersOnly.description: Changed tools whose every change is digits, separators or whitespace. Still a change: a number can be a limit.

changes.description: Per tool: kind (added | removed | changed) and, for a changed tool, every changed value with its path, before, after and, for text, a word diff.
What changed since the stored approval, field by field; null when nothing is stored.

reviewText.description: The same changes as plain lines for a person: where they came from (reported version, launch command), [-removed-] and {+added+} inside text, before → after for values, and which tools gain text about the user's approval or tool choice.

approvedVersion.description: serverInfo.version stored with the approval (the server's own word), or null.

currentVersion.description: serverInfo.version you passed now, or null.

launch.description: For npx / uvx style launches: runner, ecosystem, package, requested version or range, and pinned (an exact version in the command). null for other launches.

origin.description: Where a change came from: the versions the server reported and whether the launch command pins one.

mutationsEnabled.description: false means approve_mcp_server and revoke_mcp_server will refuse in this process.

tools.name: vet_mcp_server
tools.description:
Run WARDEN's ordered gate chain (static-scan → threat-feed → origin → pinning) over a server identity plus its advertised tools/list payload and return a recordable verdict (allow/block, 0..1 product score, findings, allowedTools/blockedTools, ruleset digest).

When to use: you have a complete server record and want the same decision a host should make before any of those tool definitions reach the model. Prefer this over calling the four gates yourself.

When NOT to use: inspecting descriptions only (call static_scan_tools — no origin/pinning); splitting tools by operator glob (classify_sensitive_tools); checking one outbound URL (check_egress_url); producing RFC 8785 bytes (canonicalize_json).

Behaviour: local, deterministic, no network. This stdio process uses the built-in 11-record threat floor (it does not fetch a signed feed) and a durable local pin store. First contact is TOOL_DEF_UNPINNED/advisory until explicitly approved. Origin defaults to allowUnknownServers=true so catalog-discovered servers are not fail-closed. Override policy when you need the host's real knobs. Does not connect to, start, or approve the target server.

Returns structured JSON matching outputSchema. Example: vet_mcp_server({ server: { id: "demo@0", name: "demo", transport: "stdio", command: "npx" }, tools: [{ name: "add", description: "Add two integers.", inputSchema: { type: "object" } }] }).

server.description: Identity of the MCP server being vetted — the host's McpServerRef, not a live connection. WARDEN never launches this command or fetches this URL.

id.description: Stable server id the host uses for pins and logs (e.g. "github@1"). Findings quote this id.

name.description: Human-facing server name. Threat-feed server-scope patterns match this field.

transport.description: How the host would launch the server. stdio uses command/args; sse/http use url. WARDEN does not open the transport.

command.description: stdio executable (e.g. "npx"). Required for a realistic stdio identity hash; omit for url transports.

args.description: stdio argv. Included in the launch-identity hash used by pinning. Omit when unused.

url.description: sse/http endpoint. Threat-feed and identity hashing see this string; this tool does not request it.

catalog.description: Remote catalog this server was discovered from. When set and policy.allowUnknownServers is false, the origin gate fail-closes. Omit for operator-declared servers.

tools.description: Exact tools/list payload (1..256 tools). Each item is name + description + inputSchema from the server. Do not filter before vetting — blockedTools is the partition.

title.description: Unmodified advertised tool title; scanned and pinned.

outputSchema.description: Unmodified output schema, including nested descriptions; scanned and pinned.

annotations.description: Advertised hints; untrusted metadata, never authorization.

name.description: Exact tool name as advertised by tools/list. Matched case-sensitively against findings.tool and against sensitive glob patterns.

description.description: Advertised description string from tools/list. This is prompt text the model would see; WARDEN scans it. Pass the server's text unmodified — rewriting it hides the injection surface.

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema object from tools/list (type/properties/required/…). Pass through as-is. WARDEN stringifies it and scans field names, descriptions, and enums. Do not invent properties the server did not advertise.

policy.description: Optional WardenPolicy overlay. Omitted keys keep the stdio defaults: blockAtSeverity=high, empty sensitiveToolPatterns, allowUnknownServers=true, pinToolDefs=true. Use classify_sensitive_tools when you only want the glob split.

blockAtSeverity.description: Block the whole connection when any non-advisory finding reaches this severity. Default high. advisory findings never block, even at info.

sensitiveToolPatterns.description: Case-insensitive * globs matched against tool names. Hits are still advertised; they go to blockedTools only when a finding also trips. For a glob-only split, call classify_sensitive_tools.

capabilityBindings.description: Operator-reviewed capabilities, bound to launch identity and complete definitions. Unbound capabilities remain unknown.

allowUnknownServers.description: When false, servers that carry server.catalog are refused by the origin gate. Default true on this stdio scanner so you can inspect catalog entries without declaring them.

requireApproval.description: Require an explicit operator approval of every advertised field and server identity. Automatic and legacy pins do not qualify. Default false.

pinToolDefs.description: When true, tool-def drift after a stored pin is fatal. Pins persist across calls and restarts; first contact stays UNPINNED/advisory. Default true.

allow.description: false when a gate was fatal or a non-advisory finding reached blockAtSeverity.

score.description: Product of per-gate scores in [0, 1]. One bad gate drags the whole server down; it is not an average.

decidedBy.description: Gate that produced the blocking decision, present only when allow is false.

gate.description: Gate that produced the finding: static-scan, threat-feed, origin, or pinning.

severity.description: Attention rank. Independent of whether the finding blocks.

code.description: Stable machine code, e.g. TOOL_DEF_INJECTION or THREAT_TOOL_MATCH.

message.description: Human-readable finding, including the matched span where a static-scan rule fired.

tool.description: Tool name the finding refers to, when the defect is per-tool rather than server-wide.

advisory.description: When true the finding is report-only: it never blocks and never costs a tool, at any blockAtSeverity.

findings.description: Accumulated findings across all gates, including advisory.

allowedTools.description: Tool names individually permitted; the host MUST also require allow=true before exposure.

blockedTools.description: Tool names quarantined; the rest of the server may still be usable.

digest.description: sha256-<base64> over the RFC 8785 canonical form of the published rule table. A recorded scan is not reproducible without this.

rulesets.description: Rule-table identity in force for this verdict. Store this with the scan.
